name: Lunar Hill Sphere
story: The boundary of the Moon's gravitational authority — roughly 60,000 km from the lunar centre. Inside this sphere, the Moon's gravity wins out over Earth's; outside, anything you leave behind drifts back toward Earth. Most stable lunar orbits live well inside, below 70% of the Hill radius, because mascon perturbation makes higher orbits unstable. The Hill sphere is also why the Moon has no natural moonlets — none can hold an orbit for long.
comparison: About 16% of the way back to Earth. The Earth-Moon L2 point sits roughly on the Hill sphere boundary on the far side — the same geometric reason both exist.
